title: Padikkal's Unbeaten 142 in Warm-Up Strengthens His Case for India's No. 3 Spot
excerpt: The left-hander anchored India's innings against the Sri Lanka Board President's XI in the team's final hit-out before the two-Test series begins in Galle on August 15.
body:
• Devdutt Padikkal struck an unbeaten 142 against the Sri Lanka Board President's XI in India's warm-up match ahead of the two-Test series starting August 15 in Galle.
  • The knock strengthens Padikkal's bid for the No. 3 batting position, which has been unsettled since Cheteshwar Pujara's departure from the Test side.
  • His main rival for the spot, Sai Sudharsan, faces a fitness test after the BCCI flagged his participation as subject to clearance.
  • Padikkal enters the series on the back of a dominant 2025-26 domestic season: 543 Ranji runs at 54.30, 725 Vijay Hazare runs at 90.63, and 464 IPL runs at a strike rate near 170.

Devdutt Padikkal made a statement that will be difficult for India's selectors to ignore, compiling an unbeaten 142 against the Sri Lanka Board President's XI in a warm-up match ahead of the two-Test series. Batting at the pivotal No. 3 position, the left-hander anchored India's innings as they closed in on the hosts' total, showing the kind of patience and shot selection that has made him one of Indian cricket's most in-demand red-ball batters.

A Century That Comes at the Right Time

Padikkal's innings was a blend of composure and controlled aggression. Having been part of the India A squad that toured Sri Lanka in June-July — where he scored 67 in the first unofficial Test and 94 in the second — the Karnataka batter has now spent considerable time acclimatizing to conditions in Sri Lanka. His 142 not out is comfortably his best score on Sri Lankan soil and comes barely a week before the first Test at the Galle International Stadium on August 15.

"There's been a lot of changes in that spot and that's not ideal. Dev comes in with a ton of runs in domestic cricket across all the formats."

— Ryan ten Doeschate, India assistant coach

The innings also carries added significance given captain Shubman Gill's need for batting stability in a series India must win to keep their World Test Championship qualification hopes alive. India have four Tests remaining in the current WTC cycle — two in Sri Lanka and two in New Zealand — and a 2-0 sweep here would put them in a commanding position.

The No. 3 Battle

India's No. 3 slot has been something of a revolving door since Cheteshwar Pujara was dropped and subsequently retired from international cricket. The team has tried Shubman Gill, Karun Nair, and Washington Sundar in the position without finding a permanent solution. The contest has narrowed to two contenders: Padikkal and Sai Sudharsan.

Sudharsan, who made his Test debut against England in 2025, has played six Tests at No. 3 but managed only 302 runs at an average of 27.45, with just two half-centuries across 11 innings. He was backed by the team management for the one-off Test against Afghanistan in June despite Padikkal's superior domestic form, with head coach Gautam Gambhir preferring to give the incumbent a longer rope.

But the equation may have shifted. The BCCI has flagged Sudharsan's participation in the Sri Lanka series as subject to fitness clearance, and Padikkal's warm-up century could not have come at a more opportune moment.

Domestic Form That Demands Selection

Padikkal's case rests on more than one innings. His 2025-26 domestic season was extraordinary by any standard. In the Ranji Trophy, he amassed 543 runs at 54.30 for Karnataka, including a mammoth 232 in the semi-final. The Vijay Hazare Trophy brought even more prolific returns — 725 runs at an average of 90.63 across nine innings. In the IPL, he was arguably the most improved cricketer of the season, hammering 464 runs at a strike rate close to 170 for Royal Challengers Bengaluru.

With 3,627 runs from 54 first-class matches, Padikkal is the more experienced red-ball cricketer compared to Sudharsan's 2,591 runs from 35 matches. His limited international Test record — two matches, 90 runs at an average of 30 — hardly does justice to a batter who has consistently dominated at every other level.

India's Test Squad and Series Outlook

India arrive in Sri Lanka without pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah, who was ruled out due to persistent discomfort in his left knee following an injury sustained during an ODI against England in Cardiff in July. Uncapped fast bowler Auqib Nabi, who took 60 wickets in the 2025-26 Ranji Trophy season to help Jammu and Kashmir win their first title, has been called up as a replacement — making him the first cricketer from the state to earn a senior Test call-up.

The squad, led by Gill with KL Rahul as vice-captain, includes Yashasvi Jaiswal, Rishabh Pant, Ravindra Jadeja, Kuldeep Yadav, Mohammed Siraj, and Prasidh Krishna among the established names. Saransh Jain, Gurnoor Brar, and Manav Suthar round out the bowling options.

What to Watch

The first Test at Galle begins on August 15, a venue where spin has historically dominated. India's spin-heavy attack — Jadeja, Kuldeep, and Suthar — should be well-suited to the conditions, but the batting order needs to deliver. If Sudharsan fails his fitness test, Padikkal's selection at No. 3 becomes almost certain. Even if Sudharsan is cleared, a 142 not out in the final audition may prove impossible to overlook. For Padikkal, a batter who has knocked loudly on the door all season, this innings might just push it wide open.
